etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English equal, from Latin aequālis. Doublet of aequalis and egal.

definitions.definition: (not comparable) The same in all respects.

quote.citation: 1705, George Cheyne, The Philosophical Principles of Religion Natural and Revealed:
quote.text: They who are not disposed to receive them may let them alone or reject them; it is equal to me.

quote.citation: 1980 July, Frank Herbert, “Dune Genesis”, in Omni‎[1], volume 2, number 10, →ISSN, →OCLC, page 74, column 2; republished as Ultimate Guide To Dune (Part 2) Book One (1:11:30)‎[2], 2017:
quote.text: I now believe that evolution, or deevolution, never ends short of death, that no society has ever achieved an absolute pinnacle, that all humans are not created equal. In fact, I believe attempts to create some abstract equalization create a morass of injustices that rebound on the equalizers. Equal justice and equal opportunity are ideals we should seek, but we should recognize that humans administer the ideals and that humans do not have equal ability.

definitions.definition: (mathematics, not comparable) Exactly identical, having the same value.

(mathematics, copulative) To be equal to, to have the same value as; to correspond to.
(transitive) To make equivalent to; to cause to match.

quote.citation: 2004, Mary Levy, Jim Kelly, Marv Levy: Where Else Would You Rather Be?:
quote.text: There was an even more remarkable attendance figure that underscores the devotion exhibited by our fans, because it was in 1991 that they set a single season in-stadium attendance record that has never been equaled.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To match in degree or some other quality, to match up to.

definitions.definition: (copulative, informal) To have as consequence, to amount to, to mean.

definitions.definition: A person or thing of equal status to others.
